sections.h2: Where is East Fishkill and how did the town take shape?
sections.html:
East Fishkill lies on the southern edge of Dutchess County, with 56.53 square miles of land. It became its own town on November 29, 1849, when about 33,000 acres were set off from the Town of Fishkill. Neighbors include Fishkill and Wappinger to the west, LaGrange to the north, Beekman and Pawling to the east, and the Putnam County towns of Philipstown and Kent to the south.

Dutch settlers were first on the land. When the railroad from Dutchess Junction to Pine Plains opened in 1869, the Hopewell hamlet grew up around the station and was renamed Hopewell Junction once a second line crossed there. The depot was built in 1873 and restored after a 1986 fire. The town's own history page says the Town Code recognizes six hamlets: Arthursburg, Fishkill Plains, Gayhead, Hopewell Junction, Peckslip and Stormville.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about East Fishkill households?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimated 29,801 residents on July 1, 2025, a gain of 0.3 percent over its 2020 base. Its QuickFacts profile paints a family-oriented, owner-heavy town.

  • Owner-occupied homes: 90.6 percent
  • Middle-of-the-range home value (2020 to 2024): $478,400
  • Middle-of-the-range household income: $138,543
  • People per household: 2.92
  • Residents who lived in the same house a year earlier: 95.3 percent
  • Average commute to work: 36.2 minutes

With 95.3 percent of residents in the same house a year earlier, most owners stay put. Gather the latest closed sales near your own street, not just a town figure.

sections.h2: Which roads and employers tie East Fishkill to the region?
sections.html:
Interstate 84 and the Taconic State Parkway both cross the town, and the Appalachian Trail passes through it. The long average commute of 36.2 minutes shows how many residents drive out of town for work, so describe highway access plainly in any listing.

The biggest local employment story is the Hudson Valley Research Park, the site once called IBM East Fishkill. It held 27 divisions and 4,700 regular employees in IBM's microelectronics business, which later became part of GlobalFoundries, and the fabrication plant now belongs to onsemi. The town's population rose from 4,778 in 1960 to 22,101 in 1990.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve East Fishkill?
sections.html:
Four districts reach into town: Arlington, Carmel, Pawling and Wappingers Central School Districts, according to the town's school district page. The town's Receiver of Taxes collects school taxes for two of them, Wappingers and Carmel.

The district decides the school tax bill and its payment calendar, so read the property's current bill before you describe the house to a buyer. The next section shows how those dates differ.

sections.h2: When are East Fishkill taxes due, and what are the penalties?
sections.html:
County and town taxes are payable once a year, in January and February without penalty. The Receiver of Taxes works from 2464 Route 52 in Hopewell Junction, next to the police station, and also collects fire, lighting and park district charges.

East Fishkill county and town tax penalties
Payment windowPenalty
January 1 to February 28None
March2 percent
April3 percent
May4 percent plus $2

Source: Town of East Fishkill Receiver of Taxes. The books close on May 31, and unpaid balances move to the Dutchess County Commissioner of Finance about June 15.

School bills run on a different clock. For 2026, Wappingers taxes were payable from September 14 to October 13, with a 2 percent penalty through October 30. Carmel taxes were payable in September, and that district alone allows a half payment with a 5 percent charge on each half. Unpaid school taxes are added to the next county and town bill.

sections.h2: How do assessments, grievances and exemptions work in East Fishkill?
sections.html:
The assessor values each parcel so school, county, town and special district taxes can be divided fairly, but the assessor does not set the tax rate. The calendar is short: taxable status date on March 1, tentative roll by May 1, Grievance Day on the 4th Tuesday of May, and the final roll on July 1, which is the roll that next year's taxes are based on.

Exemptions for seniors, veterans, firefighters and people with disabilities must be filed by March 1. STAR is filed directly with New York State, and the town asks residents not to call its office about it. Only the current tentative roll can be grieved, so a seller who thinks the value is wrong should raise it before the May hearing.

sections.h2: What septic, flood and water items come up when selling in East Fishkill?
sections.html:
Three local rules can surface during a sale, and each is easier to handle before a buyer asks.

  • Septic: owners inside the East of Hudson Watershed must have each system pumped, cleaned and visually inspected by a registered water transporter at least every five years, and file the inspection form with the Building Department.
  • Flood: East Fishkill joined FEMA's Community Rating System in October 2015 as a Class 8 community, giving a 10 percent premium discount inside the Special Flood Hazard Area and 5 percent outside it. Homeowner policies do not pay flood losses, and a new flood policy has a five-day waiting period.
  • Water and sewer: the town runs 17 water districts and 6 sewer districts, billed every three months, with a 10 percent late fee after the first month and unpaid rents re-levied on the next tax bill after November 1.

Dutchess County's Parcel Access map can show whether a property lies in a flood area, and the Building Department can supply flood data to sellers and lenders.

sections.h2: Do East Fishkill permits and records affect a sale?
sections.html:
They can. The Building Department's process starts with a complete general permit application, then a pre-site inspection, plan review, permit issuance, inspections called in by the contractor, and a final certificate once the last inspection passes. A certificate of occupancy fee applies where relevant, and the town now offers an online permit portal.

If you added a deck, finished a basement or built a garage, find the final certificate before you list. The Building Department sits on the lower level of Town Hall, with the entrance at the rear, and also houses the zoning officer and floodplain administrator.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record an East Fishkill deed?
sections.html:
The Dutchess County Clerk's fee schedule lists $45 to record a deed, $5 per page, $5 for the capital gains affidavit that accompanies form TP-584, and a $10 residential deed notification fee. State transfer tax of two dollars per $500 of price is separate and goes in with the return within 15 days of delivery.

Your closing attorney can total these and confirm what applies to your deed.

faqs.q: Is East Fishkill in Dutchess County?
faqs.a: Yes. East Fishkill sits on the southern border of Dutchess County and was split from the Town of Fishkill on November 29, 1849. Its tax office is on Route 52 in Hopewell Junction.

faqs.q: What do East Fishkill homes typically sell for?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists a middle value of $478,400 for owner-occupied homes in 2020 to 2024. That is a survey figure, so recent sales on your own street are the better guide to a price.

faqs.q: When is the last day to pay county and town taxes without a penalty?
faqs.a: February 28 is the last day without a penalty. A 2 percent charge applies in March, 3 percent in April, and 4 percent plus $2 in May, after which the county takes over collection.

faqs.q: Do East Fishkill septic systems need inspections before a sale?
faqs.a: Systems inside the East of Hudson Watershed must be pumped and inspected at least once every five years under the Town Code. Ask the Building Department whether your property lies in the blue-shaded watershed area.

faqs.q: Who sets property assessments in East Fishkill?
faqs.a: The Town Assessor values each property, and Grievance Day is the 4th Tuesday in May. The assessor cannot change the tax rate, which comes from the school, county, town and district budgets.
